key_insight: Task-aware CT projection selection improves direct hemodynamic prediction under extreme sparsity, but the selected views can be poor for image reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: Sparse CT acquisition could be tailored to wall shear stress prediction rather than anatomical reconstruction alone.
method: Generate synthetic fan-beam CTA projections from CFD simulations of intracranial aneurysms.
Train a Fourier neural operator to predict spatially resolved and spatially averaged time-averaged wall shear stress.
Compare uniform and golden-angle sampling with Gumbel-Softmax, Soft top-K, and agentic AI selection across view budgets.
evidence_signal: On synthetic CFD-derived data, agentic AI and Soft top-K achieved the lowest mean errors for spatially resolved wall shear stress, with agentic AI slightly better and both substantially outperforming fixed sampling under extreme sparsity.
watch_item: Validation on real clinical CTA is needed, and views optimized for hemodynamic prediction may not support adequate image reconstruction.
paper_title: Agentic AI Reasoning and Learned Sampling for Task-Aware Projection Selection in Sparse-View CT: Predicting Hemodynamics
